title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier-Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations in intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), the generator gpt-5-mini, and a pybatfish-style deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and permitted at most one repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Two preregistration→execution deviations materially constrain inferential reach: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidate the preregistered power calculation, which assumed independent per-condition generation; and (2) a prespecified primary comparison (GVR vs a schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable benefit in this specific artifact-grounded setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. We release and analyze the authoritative archived artifacts and describe concrete reproducible follow-ups (independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, and expanded verifier coverage).

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises safety and correctness concerns: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, workflow constraints, security predicates). Prior systems and surveys therefore recommend architectures that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects prior to execution.

We designed and preregistered a focused confirmatory evaluation to test whether a bounded GVR intervention reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding. The preregistration (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) specified a paired design on a public synthetic NetOps task bank (12 topology/policy clusters × 20 tasks = 240 tasks), a frozen analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), and two prespecified primary comparisons with Bonferroni correction. The execution artifacts are archived and authoritative (preregistration_sha256: eaedeae9aa302327e090d519a7a16f514d7fb79a472071aaf171f2f618c8ad4d).

This manuscript reports the actual executed design, precise quantitative outcomes, and an interpretation that respects preregistration and archived evidence. We explicitly highlight deviations between registered assumptions and executed semantics, explain why those deviations cause a degenerate null result in the paired analysis, and give reproducible operational recommendations for confirmatory follow-ups.
sections.related_work:
Three connected literatures motivated the study. (1) LLM failure-and-hallucination analyses show generators often produce incorrect or fabricated structured outputs for code and configuration tasks, motivating deterministic validators in downstream pipelines [10.1145/3728894; 10.36227/techrxiv.177219979.94060974/v1]. (2) Generate–Verify–Repair and constrained-decoding approaches have improved mechanically checkable properties (compilation, syntactic validity) in prior work and reduce surface-level hallucinations, but domain-level semantic correctness remains less settled [10.2139/ssrn.6754899; 10.26434/chemrxiv.15005091/v1]. (3) NetOps-specific studies emphasize verifier-driven evaluation and human-in-the-loop governance for high-stakes changes; existing intent→configuration systems incorporate validators and policy checks as practical safeguards [10.1145/3718958.3750537; 10.1145/3771567].

Our contribution differs in methodology: we preregistered a paired confirmatory experiment, archived the frozen analysis executor, and report artifact-backed episode accounting and exact per-task validator traces. Unlike benchmark-ranking studies, the present run isolates the operational question: does a single bounded GVR loop reduce verifier-detectable semantic invariant violations under the executed generation semantics and task distribution?
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and primary estimand: The preregistration (c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1) defined the primary estimand as the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (proportion difference in verifier-detected semantic-violation rate computed in paired fashion). Two primary comparisons were prespecified: (C vs A) GVR vs unconstrained generation and (C vs B) GVR vs schema-constrained decoding; family alpha = 0.05 with Bonferroni correction (per-comparison alpha = 0.025). The frozen analysis executor was paired_binary_analysis_v1.

Execution contract and concrete parameters (archived): task bank: public synthetic NetOps task bank v1, N = 240 tasks (12 clusters × 20 tasks); requested generator model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820); adapter/orchestration family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0). Crucial frozen generation semantics recorded in the preregistration and manifest: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (independent_condition_generation = false), initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 (bounded single repair attempt), maximum_model_calls = 480, execution_mode = scientific_confirmatory. The preregistration archive includes the RNG seeds, task manifest, and the adapter configuration used to execute the run (preregistration_sha256 above).

Design rationale and power plan (preregistered): The preregistered power calculation targeted an absolute paired reduction of 10 percentage points with N = 240 under independent per-condition generation assumptions. That power analysis is authoritative for the planned independent-generation design but does not apply if generation_semantics were executed as shared_initial_candidate (see Deviation paragraph below).

Scoring and oracle: The deterministic validator implements pybatfish-style checks and returns structured diagnostics (violation_count, violations list, parsed_command_count, required_command_count). Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation as implemented by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Per-task validation_before and validation_after traces are archived and authoritative for scoring decisions.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): The execution manifest records planned_episode_count = 480, completed_episode_count = 480, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 240, and model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation semantics). Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm episode accounting consistency and provider-call audit.

Primary confirmatory outcomes: The registered analysis executor computed the paired contingency table: n11 = 240 (both arms accepted), n10 = 0 (guarded only), n01 = 0 (baseline only), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Summary rates: baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; bootstrap_resamples = 10000; bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived and authoritative for these numbers.

Repair usage: For every episode the validator trace records repair_applied = false; the bounded repair loop never executed because the shared initial candidate already satisfied validator predicates for every task. Representative per-task scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json) show normalized_configuration, validation_before, validation_after, and violation_count = 0 for all episodes.

Inferential degeneracy and cause: The observed contingency of zero discordant pairs renders the paired McNemar test degenerate: no within-pair disagreements exist that could indicate an effect. The exact-test p = 1.00 and bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0] are deterministic consequences of the contingency and the preregistered analysis procedure. The executed shared_initial_candidate semantics (one generation per task reused across arms) removed stochastic independence across conditions and therefore eliminated discordance potential that the preregistered power calculation assumed.
sections.discussion:
Conservative interpretation: Under the executed shared-generation semantics and for the supplied synthetic workload and validator predicates, a bounded GVR intervention (single allowed repair attempt) produced no verifier-detectable benefit because the generator+prompting combination already produced verifier-acceptable outputs for every task. This outcome does not imply that GVR is universally unhelpful; rather, it emphasizes that evaluation semantics and oracle coverage materially determine whether GVR’s benefit can be observed.

Two artifact-supported mechanisms explain the result. First, task/verifier alignment: the synthetic task bank distribution, the generator/prompt pairing, and the validator together formed a distribution the generator satisfied deterministically. Second, the evaluation semantics (shared_initial_candidate) removed independent stochasticity between arms, preventing within-pair discordance and eliminating statistical power for the prespecified paired estimand.

Prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison and preregistration deviation: The preregistration listed two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B). The archived execution artifacts document only the adapter-configured paired experiment comparing the unconstrained baseline (A) to guarded GVR (C) under shared_initial_candidate semantics; the prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale for the omission appears in the archive. This is an explicit procedural deviation that we report as an unresolved limitation; it narrows inferential breadth and should be considered when interpreting findings.

Threats to validity: Internal validity is weakened by the preregistration→execution mismatch: the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation, which was violated. Construct validity is limited by verifier completeness: passing the deterministic validator does not guarantee absence of all operational risks outside the validator’s encoded invariants. External validity is constrained by the synthetic task bank, single generator (gpt-5-mini), single bounded repair budget, and a single verifier. Conclusion validity is limited because zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics. These threats are enumerated in the archived limitations.

Operational recommendations (artifact-grounded): (1) Re-execute the preregistered paired design with independent per-condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true) using the archived task manifest and RNG seeds to restore discordance potential. (2) Inject adversarial or golden-reference tasks (the preregistration planned 10% golden tasks) to validate verifier sensitivity. (3) Expand the generator scope to multiple models and prompt variants to measure cross-model generality. (4) Increase iterative repair budgets and record repair-iteration distributions. (5) Broaden verifier coverage (additional semantic invariants or formal/SMT hybrids) to reduce oracle incompleteness risk. The archived artifacts already contain the inputs and configuration needed to reproduce these variants deterministically.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment evaluating a bounded GVR intervention on a synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics (one shared generation per task reused across arms), every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a null paired estimate (0.0), exact McNemar p = 1.00, and paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR did not add verifier-detectable value in this specific setting because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct. Two preregistration/execution deviations materially constrain inference: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered independent-generation power assumption; and (2) a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no rationale is recorded in the archive. We therefore do not generalize beyond the specific model, prompt, task bank, verifier, repair budget, or generation semantics. The authoritative archived artifacts are released to enable deterministic reproductions and confirmatory reruns under independent-generation, adversarial injection, multi-model, and expanded-verifier regimes to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or semantic invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the archived run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms). This design reduced model-call cost but also removed per-arm stochastic variation and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic verifier does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
